AbstractText.Label: Context
AbstractText.content: KCNJ5 mutation is a major cause of aldosterone-producing adenoma (APA). The development of APA apart from KCNJ5 mutation is less investigated.

AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: To investigate other mechanisms affecting aldosterone secretion apart from KCNJ5.

AbstractText.Label: Patients and Methods
AbstractText.content: Six pairs of KCNJ5-mutated, high and low aldosterone-secreting APAs, five non-KCNJ5-mutated APAs and four normal adrenal glands were assayed by Affymetrix Genechip Human Transcriptome Array 2.0. A total of 113 APA samples were investigated to explore the expression of GSTA1. H295R cells were used to verify the function of GSTA1.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: Glutathione-S-transferase A1 (GSTA1) was the top gene down-regulated in high aldosterone KCNJ5 mutated APAs. GSTA1 was also down-regulated in KCNJ5 mutated APAs compared with wild-type KCNJ5 APAs. Accordingly, mutant KCNJ5 decreased GSTA1 mRNA and protein expression levels. GSTA1 overexpression suppressed aldosterone secretion whether in wild type or mutant KCNJ5 H295R cells. Adding etacrynic acid or silencing of GSTA1 increased aldosterone secretion by increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS), superoxide, H2O2 levels and Ca2+ influx. The expression of the transcription factors NR4A1, NR4A2, and CAMK1 and intracellular Ca2+ were significantly upregulated by GSTA1 inhibition. NADPH oxidase inhibitor, H2O2 scavenger, blocking calmodulin or blocking calcium channels could significantly reduced aldosterone secretion in GSTA1-inhibited cells.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: (1) GSTA1 expression is reversely correlated with aldosterone level in KCNJ5-mutated APAs; (2) GSTA1 regulates aldosterone secretion by ROS and Ca2+ signaling. (3) KCNJ5 mutation downregulates GSTA1 expression, and overexpression of GSTA1 reverses increased aldosterone in KCNJ5-mutated adrenal cells.
